en: chief director; chairman of the board of directors

examples.en: The chairman gave a congratulatory speech at the graduation.
The chairman of our school was a teacher long ago.
I made an appointment to meet the hospital chairman.
A new chairman will be chosen next month.
The staff passed on their thanks to the chairman.
The chairman's office is at the end of the third floor.

explain: 학교, 병원, 재단처럼 이사회가 있는 곳에서 쓰는 직함이에요. 회사 대표를 가리키는 '사장'과 달라요. 부를 때는 '이사장님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The chairman came to the school today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이사장'을 높여 부르거나 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The respectful way to address or refer to the chairman.

phrases.en: That person is the chairman of a scholarship foundation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이사장' 앞에 일하는 곳을 붙여서 어디의 이사장인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the organization before the title says which body the chairman leads.

phrases.en: My uncle became the chairman of a hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이사장이 되다'로 그 자리에 오르는 일을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '이사장이 되다' describes taking up the post.

explain_en: It is a title used in places that have a board of directors, such as schools, hospitals, and foundations. It differs from '사장', which refers to a company head. When addressing the person, say '이사장님'.

examples.en: That painter passed away last winter.
My teacher, whom I respected, passed away last year.

examples.ko: 작고하신 선생님의 책을 다시 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I am rereading the books of my late teacher.

examples.ko: 그분이 작고한 지 벌써 십 년이 지났어요.
examples.en: It has already been ten years since that person passed away.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 작고하기 전에 마지막 소설을 썼어요.
examples.en: That writer wrote a last novel before passing away.

examples.ko: 아버지 친구분이 갑자기 작고하셔서 장례식에 다녀왔어요.
examples.en: My father's friend suddenly passed away, so I went to the funeral.

explain: '돌아가시다'보다 격식 있고 글 같은 말이라서 신문이나 추모 글에서 많이 봐요. 주로 화가, 작가, 학자처럼 존경받는 분에게 쓰고, 일상 대화에서 가족 이야기를 할 때는 보통 '돌아가시다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 작고한 작가의 작품을 모은 전시회가 열려요.
phrases.en: An exhibition of a late writer's works is opening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 세상을 떠난 존경받는 사람을 글에서 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in writing to introduce a respected person who has passed away.

phrases.example: 그 화가는 작고하기 전에 마지막 작품을 남겼어요.
phrases.en: The painter left a final work before he passed away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상을 떠나기 바로 전의 때를 말할 때 연결형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The connective form for the time just before someone's death.

phrases.example: 작고 후에 그의 그림값이 크게 올랐어요.
phrases.en: After his death, the price of his paintings rose greatly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상을 떠난 뒤의 일을 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to talk about what happened after someone's death.

explain_en: It is more formal and bookish than '돌아가시다', so you often see it in newspapers and tribute writing. It is mostly used for respected people such as painters, writers and scholars. In everyday talk about family, people usually say '돌아가시다'.

examples.ko: 오늘 행사에는 저명인사 여러 분이 참석해요.
examples.en: Several prominent figures are attending today's event.
He is regarded as a prominent figure in the industry.
It was a talk by a notable person, so the seats filled fast.
I took a photo with some distinguished people.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 저명인사가 된 졸업생이 많아요.
examples.en: This school has many graduates who became prominent figures.

examples.ko: 저명인사라고 해서 모두 친절한 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Not every prominent person is kind.

explain: 학계, 정치, 문화처럼 한 분야에서 이름이 널리 알려진 사람을 점잖게 부르는 말이에요. 연예인에게는 보통 '유명인'이나 '연예인'이라고 하고, '저명인사'는 격식 있는 자리나 기사에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: A prominent scholar is giving a lecture today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저명한'은 분야 이름과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 저명한 is often paired with a field or role.

phrases.en: Many prominent figures attended the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람을 가리킬 때 복수형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Plural form for referring to several people.

phrases.en: Famous people often come to that shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저명인사'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more casual than 저명인사.

explain_en: It is a polished way to call someone widely known in a field such as academia, politics or culture. For entertainers people usually say '유명인' or '연예인'; '저명인사' suits formal occasions and articles.

examples.ko: 대통령이 외국 대사를 접견했다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was news that the president had received a foreign ambassador.

examples.ko: 총리는 오후에 방한한 대표단을 접견할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The prime minister plans to receive the visiting delegation in the afternoon.
The president is receiving a guest right now.

examples.ko: 장관이 직접 시민 대표를 접견하는 자리가 마련됐어요.
examples.en: A meeting was arranged where the minister personally receives citizen representatives.
The ambassador had an audience with the king and handed over his credentials.

examples.ko: 가족이 수감자를 접견할 수 있는 시간이 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The times when family can meet an inmate are fixed.

explain: 높은 직위의 사람이 공식적으로 손님이나 방문객을 만나는 일에 써서, 친구를 만날 때 '만나다' 대신 쓰지 않아요. 주어는 보통 대통령, 장관, 사장 같은 사람이에요.

phrases.en: The president said he had met with the delegation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 공식 만남을 알릴 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style way to announce an official meeting.

phrases.en: We showed the guests to the reception room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 손님을 만나는 방을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The room used for officially receiving guests.

phrases.en: After the audience ended, they held a press conference.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 만남이 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the formal meeting is over.

explain_en: It is used when a high-ranking person formally receives a guest or visitor, so you wouldn't use it instead of '만나다' for meeting a friend. The subject is usually someone like a president, minister or company head.

examples.ko: 친구 아버지가 돌아가셔서 장례식장에 조문하러 갔어요.
examples.en: My friend's father passed away, so I went to the funeral hall to pay my respects.
Many people visited the memorial altar to pay their condolences.
I decided to go and offer condolences together with my coworkers.

examples.ko: 조문할 때는 검은색 옷을 입는 게 예의예요.
examples.en: It is polite to wear black when paying condolences.

examples.ko: 멀리 있어서 직접 조문하지 못해 마음이 무거워요.
examples.en: I'm far away and couldn't attend in person, so my heart feels heavy.
Our professor passed away, so his students paid their respects at the funeral altar.

explain: 보통 '조문하러 가다'처럼 써요. 직접 가지 못하면 '부의금을 보내다'나 '위로 문자를 보내다'처럼 말해요. '문상하다'와 거의 같게 쓰지만, 뉴스나 공식적인 글에서는 '조문'이 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 내일 회사 동료와 함께 조문하러 가요.
phrases.en: Tomorrow I'm going to pay my respects with a coworker.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)러 가다'를 붙여 직접 찾아가는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -(으)러 가다 expresses going in person to pay respects.

phrases.en: I paid my respects at my friend's mother's funeral altar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조문하다'와 거의 같게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used almost the same as 조문하다.

phrases.example: 빈소에서 조문하고 유가족에게 위로의 말을 전했어요.
phrases.en: I paid my respects at the funeral altar and offered words of comfort to the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조문하는 장소를 함께 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the place where condolences are paid.
phrases.en_equiv: pay respects at the funeral altar

explain_en: It is usually used as '조문하러 가다' (go to pay condolences). If you can't go in person, people say '부의금을 보내다' (send condolence money) or '위로 문자를 보내다' (send a message of comfort). It is used almost the same as '문상하다', but news and formal writing often use '조문'.

examples.en: My grandfather farmed in the countryside.
My grandfather taught me Chinese characters.

examples.ko: 조부 댁에 가면 항상 맛있는 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: When I go to my grandfather's house, I always eat delicious food.
I have to write my grandfather's name on the form.
My grandfather passed away last year.

examples.ko: 거실에 조부께서 쓰신 글씨가 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A piece of calligraphy my grandfather wrote hangs in the living room.

explain: 조부는 아버지의 아버지를 격식 있게 부르는 말이에요. 어머니 쪽 할아버지는 '외조부'라고 해서 구분해요. 평소에는 '할아버지'를 쓰고, 조부는 서류나 어른 앞에서 정중하게 말할 때 써요. 상대방의 할아버지를 높일 때는 '조부님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My grandfather turned eighty this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조부'에 '-님'을 붙여 더 높이는 말이에요. 어른 앞에서 쓰면 정중해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -님 to 조부 makes it more respectful, suitable in front of elders.

phrases.en: My grandparents live in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 할아버지와 할머니를 함께 높여 부르는 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal, respectful word for grandfather and grandmother together.

phrases.en: My grandfather takes a walk every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조부와 같은 사람을 가리키지만, 평소 말할 때 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the same person as 조부, but is the everyday, casual word.

explain_en: 조부 is the formal word for one's father's father. The maternal grandfather is called 외조부, which keeps the two apart. In daily life Koreans say 할아버지, and use 조부 on documents or when speaking politely to elders. To honor someone else's grandfather, you say 조부님.

examples.en: The courtiers bowed their heads before the king.

examples.ko: 그는 손님에게 연신 머리를 조아리며 사과했어요.
examples.en: He apologized to the customer, bowing his head again and again.
Even though he bowed and begged forgiveness, it was no use.

examples.ko: 할머니는 부처님 앞에서 머리를 조아리고 기도하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother bowed her head in front of the Buddha and prayed.
You don't have to bow your head that much.

examples.ko: 한 번만 봐 달라고 머리를 조아려서라도 부탁해 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll even bow my head and beg them to let it go just once.

explain: '머리를 조아리다'처럼 거의 이 형태로 써요. '고개를 숙이다'보다 더 깊이, 여러 번 숙이는 느낌이고 굽실거리는 부정적인 느낌이 들 수도 있어요.

phrases.en: He bowed his head and begged for forgiveness.
phrases.nuance_ko: '머리를 조아리다'와 비슷한 말이고, 둘 다 깊이 숙이는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '머리를 조아리다'; both mean bowing deeply.

phrases.example: 그녀는 머리를 조아리며 도와 달라고 부탁했어요.
phrases.en: She bowed her head and begged for help.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 이어서 절박하게 부탁하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with '-며' to show someone pleading earnestly.
phrases.en_equiv: to plead with a bowed head

phrases.example: 직원이 손님 앞에서 계속 머리를 조아렸어요.
phrases.en: The employee kept bowing his head in front of the customer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 해요체예요. '조아리다'는 보통 '머리를'이나 '고개를'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past polite form; 조아리다 is usually used with '머리를' or '고개를'.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '머리를 조아리다'. It feels deeper and more repeated than '고개를 숙이다', and can sound servile.

examples.ko: 부산 지부장이 이번 주에 본사에 와요.
examples.en: The Busan branch manager is coming to headquarters this week.
I sent the report to the branch manager.

examples.ko: 새로 온 지부장은 직원들 이야기를 잘 들어요.
examples.en: The newly arrived branch manager listens well to the staff.
Our association's branch head is chosen by vote.
The branch manager changed, so the atmosphere changed.
My father works as a branch chief at an association.

explain: 지부장은 본부 아래 지역 지부를 이끄는 사람이에요. 은행이나 가게의 '지점장'과 비슷하지만, 지부장은 협회나 노동조합, 단체의 지역 조직에서 더 자주 써요. 부르는 말은 '지부장님'이에요.

phrases.en: The union branch head talked with the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노동조합의 지역 조직을 이끄는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the person who leads a local branch of a labor union.

phrases.en: There is a branch managers' meeting tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 지부장이 모이는 회의를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A meeting where several branch heads gather.

phrases.en: The new branch manager is coming next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리에 새로 온 사람을 말할 때 앞에 '새'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 새 in front to talk about someone newly in the position.

explain_en: 지부장 is the person who leads a regional branch under a headquarters. It is similar to 지점장 for a bank or shop, but 지부장 is used more often for regional units of associations, unions, and organizations. The way to address one is 지부장님.

examples.en: During the holiday I go to my hometown to visit my parents.
I'll go visit you next week, teacher.

examples.ko: 선생님 댁에 찾아뵈었더니 사모님이 차를 내 주셨어요.
examples.en: When I visited my teacher's home, his wife served me tea.
I'm sorry I haven't been able to visit you for so long.
At New Year it is polite to visit the elders.

examples.ko: 직접 찾아봬야 하는데 전화로 먼저 인사드려요.
examples.en: I should visit in person, but I'll greet you by phone first.

explain: 윗사람을 만나러 가는 것을 자기를 낮춰서 말하는 표현이라, 부모님, 선생님, 어른께만 써요. '찾아뵙다'도 같은 뜻으로 자주 쓰고, 해요체는 '찾아뵈어요'와 '찾아봬요' 둘 다 가능해요. 친구나 아랫사람에게는 그냥 '찾아가다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I visited my grandmother at New Year and greeted her.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾아뵈다와 같은 뜻으로 더 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and the more commonly used form.

phrases.en: I'm going to visit my teacher tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾아뵈다의 짧은 해요체로 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The short polite-form conjugation, common in conversation.

phrases.en: When I have time, I'd like to visit my professor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람을 만나고 싶다는 바람을 공손하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Politely expresses a wish to visit a senior person.

explain_en: It humbly describes going to see someone senior, so use it only for parents, teachers and elders. '찾아뵙다' is also commonly used with the same meaning, and the polite form can be either '찾아뵈어요' or '찾아봬요'. For friends or juniors, just use '찾아가다'.

examples.en: I exchanged names with someone I met for the first time.
Shall we at least introduce ourselves to each other?
I introduced myself to my neighbor and we also exchanged contact numbers.
After exchanging names on the blind date, we had tea.
I ended up exchanging names with the man in the next seat on the train.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 통성명이 끝나자 명함을 주고받았어요.
examples.en: Once the two finished introducing themselves, they exchanged business cards.

explain: 서로 이름을 알려 주며 처음 인사하는 것을 말하고, 'A와/과 통성명하다'처럼 상대와 함께 해요. 조금 격식 있고 예스러운 느낌이라 일상 대화에서는 '인사하다'나 '이름을 묻다'를 더 많이 써요. 처음 만난 사이에서 이름을 주고받는 장면에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: We've exchanged names, so we say hello when we meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름을 서로 알게 된 정도의 가벼운 관계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a light relationship where people just know each other's names.

phrases.en: Let's start by introducing ourselves and then talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화 전에 먼저 이름을 알려 주자고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to suggest sharing names before starting to talk.

phrases.en: I asked the person next to me for their name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural expression in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It means greeting each other for the first time by telling each other your names, and it is used with a partner, as in 'A와/과 통성명하다'. It sounds a bit formal and old-fashioned, so in daily talk people use '인사하다' or '이름을 묻다' more. It suits scenes where strangers first exchange names.
